title: The European Union: Economic Integration
text: The European Union's single market, one of the most advanced examples of economic integration in the world, allows free movement of goods, services, capital, and persons between member states. The EU Customs Union eliminates tariffs on trade between members and imposes a common external tariff. The Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) established the euro as a common currency, adopted by 20 member states. EU competition law prevents anticompetitive practices. The EU budget is financed primarily through member states' GNI contributions and VAT-based contributions. The EU also has a common agricultural policy (CAP) and cohesion funds to reduce regional economic disparities.
